prompt.context_jp: 鷹野___といえば、隣のベンチで悠然と缶コーヒーを傾け…
prompt.prompt_jp: 鷹野___といえば、隣のベンチで悠然と缶コーヒーを傾け、鶸田の慌てぶりを他人事のように眺めている。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle that fits the contrastive 'as for X' pattern.

feedback.correct_en: は shifts the topic to Takano by contrast with Hiwada, who was just described as panicking. 〜はといえば is a set contrastive-topic pattern.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would present Takano as new information, breaking the contrast with Hiwada. で doesn't form this idiomatic pattern.

contrast_examples.jp: 彼はといえば、何もしていなかった。
contrast_examples.en: As for him (by contrast), he was doing nothing.

prompt.context_jp: 彼女の落ち着きよう___常に鶸田を安心させると同時に、なぜだかいっそう焦らせもした。
prompt.prompt_jp: 彼女の落ち着きよう___常に鶸田を安心させると同時に…焦らせもした。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle best fitting here.

feedback.correct_en: は marks 彼女の落ち着きよう as the topic the narrator is characterizing — a general comment about how her calmness functions. The sentence is explanatory, not announcing a new event.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would read as a one-time 'her calmness (just now) reassured him,' but the sentence makes a habitual/general statement with 常に.

contrast_examples.en: Her smile (new, perceptual) came into view.

prompt.context_jp: 電波の四本立ちを確認した瞬間、こわばっていた肩___わずかに落ちた。
prompt.prompt_jp: こわばっていた肩___わずかに落ちた。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle to describe this momentary observation.

feedback.correct_en: が marks the shoulders dropping as a newly observed, momentary event — a sensed change at that instant. This 'event-reporting' use is a classic が context.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would turn the shoulders into a known topic for general commentary, losing the sense of a sudden observable change.

contrast_examples.en: As for tears, I won't shed them anymore (contrast).

prompt.context_jp: 通信品質___思ったよりも悪く、相手の言葉が細切れに届く。
prompt.prompt_jp: 通信品質___思ったよりも悪く、相手の言葉が細切れに届く。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle that fits.

feedback.correct_en: は sets 通信品質 as the topic the narrator is evaluating ('as for the connection quality, it was worse than expected'). Notice the second clause uses が for the newly-observed fragmented speech.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would frame the connection quality as newly introduced info, but it's actually the known situation being commented on.

contrast_examples.jp: 天気は悪かったが、気分は良かった。
contrast_examples.en: The weather was bad, but my mood was good (contrastive topic).

prompt.context_jp: 彼女___鶸田が席を外したことなど知る由もなく、いつもの表情で椅子に腰を下ろした。
prompt.prompt_jp: 彼女___…椅子に腰を下ろした。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle.

feedback.correct_en: は marks 彼女 as the continuing topic — the sentence describes multiple things about her (unaware + sat down). Note the embedded 鶸田が uses が for the subordinate-clause subject.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would make 彼女 feel newly introduced, but Takano has been the topic across these sentences.

contrast_examples.jp: 彼女は何も知らずに座った。
そのとき彼女が入ってきた。
contrast_examples.en: At that moment she came in (new entrance).

prompt.context_jp: 貝塚のほう___相変わらず、鷹野の物腰の柔らかさに惹き込まれるように身を乗り出している。
prompt.prompt_jp: 貝塚のほう___相変わらず…身を乗り出している。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle.

feedback.correct_en: は with 〜のほう sets up a contrast — Nakano was just described sensing something odd, while Kaizuka (by contrast) is leaning in enchanted. 〜のほうは is a canonical contrastive topic.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would announce Kaizuka as new info, breaking the contrast with Nakano that the structure ほう signals.

contrast_examples.jp: 兄は賛成、弟のほうは反対だった。
contrast_examples.en: The older brother agreed; the younger one, by contrast, opposed.

prompt.context_jp: 鷹野のカメラの向こうを、色鮮やかなシャツを着た若い男___通り過ぎていったのだった。
prompt.prompt_jp: 色鮮やかなシャツを着た若い男___通り過ぎていった。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle.

feedback.correct_en: が introduces the young man as brand-new information — he just appeared on camera for the first time. This is the classic 'event-presenting' が.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would imply he was already an established topic, which he isn't. を can't mark the subject of 通り過ぎる here (the location を is already taken by カメラの向こうを).

contrast_examples.jp: 知らない人が通りかかった。

prompt.context_jp: 貝塚の頬___うっすらと赤みが差し、目の縁が湿っていた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 貝塚の頬___うっすらと赤みが差し…
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle.

feedback.correct_en: には marks the location where redness appeared, with は adding topic/contrast nuance. 赤みが差す takes が for the appearing thing and に for the surface it appears on.
feedback.incorrect_en: がは and をは are not valid particle combinations in standard Japanese.

contrast_examples.jp: 顔には笑みが浮かんだ。
contrast_examples.en: On his face, a smile appeared.
Tears welled up in his eyes.

prompt.context_jp: 店を出ようとした鶸田を、鷹野___呼び止める。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle.

feedback.correct_en: が marks Takano as the new-action agent in this scene-shifting sentence — her stopping him is the newly introduced event. Note Hiwada already has を as the object being stopped.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would read oddly as topic-marking when the sentence is reporting a sudden action.

contrast_examples.jp: そのとき母が呼び止めた。
contrast_examples.en: At that moment Mother called out to stop him.

prompt.context_jp: 「なんで？」「だって… 同期だから」
prompt.prompt_jp: 同期だから、一緒に捜す。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle best fits 'why?' being answered with new reasoning?

feedback.correct_en: だから presents the reason newly ('because we're dōki'). This is a reasoning connector, matching the explanation she offers Karasumori.
feedback.incorrect_en: なのに would set up a contrast ('even though we're dōki…'), which contradicts the supportive tone.

contrast_examples.en: Even though we're friends, he's cold.

prompt.context_jp: 「そこを動かないでください 今から___にまいります」
prompt.prompt_jp: 今からお___にまいります。
prompt.prompt_en: Fill in the word that makes 'I'll come to pick you up' in humble register.

feedback.correct_en: お迎えにまいります = 'I'll come to pick you up' in humble language. まいる is the humble form of 行く/来る, pairing with 迎え for picking someone up.
feedback.incorrect_en: お送り = seeing off/sending (opposite direction). お届け = delivering an item, not picking up a person.

contrast_examples.jp: 駅までお迎えに参ります。
contrast_examples.en: I'll come pick you up at the station.

prompt.context_jp: 「君が___必要だから」
prompt.prompt_en: Fill in the adverb meaning 'absolutely / no matter what.'

feedback.correct_en: どうしても means 'absolutely, by all means' — expressing strong necessity. 'We need you no matter what' is exactly the emotional emphasis the boss wants.
feedback.incorrect_en: どうやって = 'how (by what method),' a question word. どうにか = 'somehow, manage to,' which weakens the statement rather than strengthening it.

contrast_examples.jp: どうしても諦められない。
contrast_examples.en: I just can't give up (no matter what).

prompt.context_jp: 「オフィスにいるのも___ですよ」
prompt.prompt_jp: オフィスにいるのも___ですよ。
prompt.prompt_en: Fill in Takano's punchline word.

feedback.correct_en: 仕事 ('work/the job') lands the deadpan point: simply being present at the office is itself part of the job. Fits the chapter's theme about physical presence.
feedback.incorrect_en: 遊び or 趣味 contradict the context — she's convincing Tsubatani to return to work, not play.

contrast_examples.jp: 顔を出すのも仕事のうちだ。
contrast_examples.en: Showing your face is part of the job.

prompt.context_jp: 「専ら ＰＣと___しているだけです」
prompt.prompt_en: Fill in the expression meaning 'staring intently at.'

feedback.correct_en: にらめっこ ('staring contest') is the common idiom for being glued to a screen or document. Takano means she just stares at her PC all day.
feedback.incorrect_en: かくれんぼ = hide-and-seek; おしゃべり = chatting — neither fits 'facing the PC all day.'

contrast_examples.jp: 書類とにらめっこしている。
子供がかくれんぼをする。

prompt.context_jp: 「___足をつけて いい仕事して 満足できるんだね」
prompt.prompt_jp: ___足をつけていい仕事ができる。
prompt.prompt_en: Fill in the idiom meaning 'with both feet on the ground / grounded.'

feedback.correct_en: 地に足をつける ('to plant one's feet on the ground') means to be grounded/realistic. Kunio praises small-company workers for being down-to-earth.
feedback.incorrect_en: 手に or 顔に don't form this idiom — the body-part image is specifically '地 (ground)' for grounded-ness.

contrast_examples.jp: 地に足のついた仕事をする。

prompt.context_jp: 「人___っていうのは 服の柄のことじゃないよ」
prompt.prompt_jp: 人___っていうのは、服の柄のことじゃないよ。
prompt.prompt_en: Fill in the compound meaning 'character/personality.'

feedback.correct_en: 人柄 (hitogara) = 'personal character.' The joke is that Takano read 柄 as 'pattern (of clothes)' instead of as part of 人柄.
feedback.incorrect_en: 人間 means 'human' and 人気 means 'popularity' — neither matches Hiwada's correction about the compliment being about character.

contrast_examples.jp: あの服の柄がかわいい。

prompt.context_jp: 「燕谷くん 落ち着いて その人___同僚よ」
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle.

feedback.correct_en: は identifies 'that person' as the topic and provides new predicate information ('is a colleague'). This is the classic 'X は Y だ' identificational statement.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would emphasize that THAT person (and no one else) is the colleague — an exhaustive reading that doesn't match the reassurance tone.

contrast_examples.en: That person is a senior colleague (identifying).

prompt.context_jp: 静けさに慣れきった耳に、着信音___妙に鋭く響いた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 着信音___妙に鋭く響いた。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle.

feedback.correct_en: が marks the ringtone as newly intruding information — it suddenly cuts through the silence as an event. Sudden sensory events in narrative description typically take が.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would turn the ringtone into an already-known topic, losing the surprising intrusion feel.

prompt.context_jp: 貝塚の目にはまだ、その光景の意味が理解できていなかった。
prompt.prompt_en: Which continuation sounds most natural following that sentence?

choices.text: 中野も同じで、彼女は口元に手を当て…
中野が同じで、彼女は口元に手を当て…
中野も同じが、彼女は口元に手を当て…

feedback.correct_en: 中野も同じで uses も to add Nakano to the same situation as Kaizuka — 'Nakano too was the same.' This matches the original.
feedback.incorrect_en: 中野が同じで loses the 'also' nuance and sounds like Nakano is being newly singled out. 中野も同じが is ungrammatical — が doesn't attach to a noun predicate here.

contrast_examples.jp: 兄もそうで、弟もそうだった。
contrast_examples.en: The older brother was like that too, and so was the younger one.
It was Father who was the same (exhaustive, odd here).

prompt.context_jp: 鶸田が商談で深く謝罪し、お願いする場面
prompt.prompt_en: Which phrasing is most natural for the business apology/request Hiwada is making?

choices.text: 本当に申し訳ございませんでした。チャンスをいただけるなら全力で頑張ります。
マジでごめんなさい。チャンスくれたら全力で頑張ります。
本当にすみませんでした。チャンスをもらうなら全力で頑張ります。

feedback.correct_en: 申し訳ございませんでした is the standard deep business apology; いただけるなら uses humble-receiving conditional, appropriate when asking a client for a chance.
feedback.incorrect_en: マジで/ごめんなさい/くれたら are casual registers wrong for a client meeting. もらうなら lacks humble register and the conditional nuance of 'if you would grant.'

contrast_examples.jp: ご検討いただけますと幸いです。
contrast_examples.en: We would be grateful if you would consider it.

contrast_examples.jp: 考えてくれたら嬉しい。
contrast_examples.en: I'd be happy if you'd consider it (casual).

prompt.context_jp: 烏森の決め台詞「俺は何事も完璧にやり遂げたいんだ」
prompt.prompt_en: Which version sounds most natural for Karasumori's self-declaration?

choices.text: 俺は何事も完璧にやり遂げたいんだ。
俺が何事も完璧にやり遂げたいんだ。
俺は何事が完璧にやり遂げたいんだ。

feedback.correct_en: 俺は sets 'I' as the topic for a self-definition. 何事も ('anything/everything') is the right 'any-X' pattern with も.
feedback.incorrect_en: 俺が would read as exhaustive/contrastive ('I, and no one else'), unnatural for a general self-description. 何事が is wrong — 何事も is the fixed form for 'anything.'

contrast_examples.jp: 私は何事にも全力を尽くす。
contrast_examples.en: I give my all to anything.
Who's going to do it perfectly? (exhaustive が)

prompt.context_jp: 鷹野が学生に語る場面
prompt.prompt_en: Which phrasing sounds most natural?

choices.text: 価値が高いものは大きいものと思いがちですが…
価値は高いものが大きいものと思いがちですが…
価値が高いものが大きいものと思いがちですが…

feedback.correct_en: 価値が高いもの (relative clause: 'things that have high value') uses が inside the modifier, then は topicalizes the whole phrase. This is the natural structure.
feedback.incorrect_en: Swapping は and が breaks the relative-clause structure. Double-が repeats the subject marker and sounds unnatural in this topic-comment sentence.

contrast_examples.jp: 値段が高いものは質もいい。
contrast_examples.en: Things with high prices (also) have good quality.

contrast_examples.jp: 値段は高いが、質は悪い。
contrast_examples.en: The price is high, but the quality is bad (contrast).

prompt.context_jp: 同期の関係が崩れていく話題
prompt.prompt_en: Which phrasing is most natural for 'as soon as pay gaps appear, people quickly fall out'?

choices.text: 給料に差がつくと、途端に仲悪くなりますもんね。
給料で差がつくと、途端に仲悪くなりますもんね。
給料に差をつけると、途端に仲悪くなりますもんね。

feedback.correct_en: 差がつく ('a gap appears/forms') takes に to mark the domain where the gap arises — 給料に差がつく. This is the natural collocation.
feedback.incorrect_en: 給料で would mark 給料 as means, not domain. 差をつける means 'to deliberately create a gap,' changing the agent to the person — but the original describes the gap arising naturally.
